name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district, among Minnesota's most Republican seats
Fischbach's incumbency and 2-to-1 fundraising edge ($1.29M to $537K)
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97%
No public polling; Osberg's $537K haul is active but insufficient
model.rationale: The district's 18-point Republican lean, Fischbach's incumbent advantage and clear money lead, and markets pricing a Republican hold at roughly 97% all point the same way, with no polling or expert ratings suggesting the race is competitive.
model.watch: Only a late surge of outside spending against Fischbach paired with a district-wide shift far beyond recent elections would put the outcome in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Minnesota's 7th District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly 18 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Michelle Fischbach is seeking re-election and holds a clear financial edge, having raised about $1.29 million to challenger Erik Osberg's $537,000, along with a large cash-on-hand advantage. No independent polls of the general election are available, and no expert race ratings have been issued.

Prediction markets give the Republican side roughly a 97 percent chance of holding the seat. Osberg has run an active campaign for a challenger in such a heavily Republican district, but outside spending on either side is essentially absent and the fundamentals give Fischbach a commanding structural position. The seat remains firmly in Republican hands absent a dramatic shift far larger than recent elections here have shown.
